newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ monetary conditions index up a touch in Jan-BT.
newsitem.headline: NZ monetary conditions index up a touch in Jan-BT.

text.p: Bankers Trust New Zealand said on Tuesday its monetary conditions index rose slightly to average 125 in January from 123 in December.
"The assumed MCI for the March 1997 quarter, based on the RBNZ's December Monetary Policy Statement, is 123," BT said.
It said that monetary conditions were unusually stable in January, in contrast to more volatile monetary conditions in late 1996.
"The stability of recent monetary conditions may in part reflect the holiday period and the lack of New Zealand data (although both the CPI and GDP data were stronger than expected)," BT said.

"More likely, we think the stability reflects the currency/interest rate trade-off made explicit by the RBNZ in the December MPS -- a 2.0 percent move in the TWI equals a 100 basis point move in 90-day bank bill rates."
BT said the market's focus on this trade-off had increased.
With recent data unlikely to have significantly altered the RBNZ's inflation outlook, the market had seen little need to move away from the RBNZ's prescribed "level" of monetary conditions.
